title: LastBuy: every unit justified before the final order
description: LastBuy helps an industrial thermal-camera manufacturer's service supply-chain director verify a final semiconductor purchase before a non-cancelable order. Four scoped Microsoft Foundry specialists examine engineering applicability, component-specific service obligations, physical supply and supplier commitment. Exact source quotations and critical-fact checks feed a deterministic allocation solver. Four distinct human roles approve the source-bound plan; an isolated exporter rechecks authority and reconciles uncertain writes. Real Foundry, Azure Functions, SQL and Blob executions are recorded. In the example enterprise case, 22,000 units of protected demand require a 10,000-unit buy after stock reconciliation, producing a $640,000 modeled commitment difference at an assumed $80 unit price. A separate public market screen verifies real onsemi pricing and discontinuance evidence; those prices are not substituted into the historical example. Live testing exposed historical stock being selected as current; new approval/export gates reject that evidence. A customer pilot will measure planner effort and coverage quality, targeting at least 50% less active reconciliation time. The public market calculator is deterministic; the Foundry workflow is the agent submission.

beats.screen: Public market evidence: AP0202AT2L00XPGA0-DR notice and 250-unit INR subtotal
beats.narration: A real onsemi image processor reaches last-time-buy on 7 October. The manufacturer's notice makes orders non-cancelable and non-returnable. On 20 September, the distributor listed 250 units at 200,119 rupees and 92 paise before additional charges. Public stock is not a guaranteed allocation.

beats.screen: Completed Foundry case LTB-CLOUD-RELEASE-7; show scenario label
beats.narration: LastBuy addresses the enterprise decision behind such a deadline. This separate example is a thermal-camera OEM's proposed final buy: 18,000 units at an assumed 80 dollars each. The business records are examples; the four-stage Foundry execution is real and already completed.

beats.screen: Detector warranty, component-specific amendment and engineering source records
beats.narration: Engineering checks released compatibility. Service checks which component the contract actually covers. A ten-year detector warranty does not establish processor coverage. The component-specific service amendment protects 22,000 units of repair demand. Each accepted fact carries an exact source quotation.

beats.screen: Quantity bridge and recorded four specialist results
beats.narration: Supply removes duplicated custody, incompatible units and quarantine from 14,000 reported units. With 8,000 eligible units and 4,000 inbound, the deterministic solver requires a 10,000-unit buy. The 640,000-dollar difference is modeled commitment, not achieved customer savings. Models explain evidence; the solver calculates quantity.

beats.screen: Local captured-response case LTB-LIVE-CURRENT-BALANCE-20260920: source, blocker and engineering approval view
beats.narration: Testing caught a real failure: the model selected 6,000 opening units even though the source stated 4,800 current units. Replaying that captured response now produces a historical-evidence blocker. The calculation is visibly provisional, and an engineering approver cannot approve or export it. We preserved the original failure rather than relabeling it as success.

beats.screen: PDF architecture and authority diagram; current cloud planner role
beats.narration: Durable Functions persists the workflow. Engineering, service, finance and procurement must approve the same source and plan version. The current cloud user is planner-only. The model has no purchasing tool, and the export worker has its own identity.

beats.screen: Recorded cloud export verification: CREATE and RECOVER, each one row and same repeated receipt
beats.narration: The real cloud exporter was tested against a separate ERP simulation. A normal export and a preseeded lost-response case each ended with one requisition; repeated requests returned the same receipt. A legacy-approved historical-stock fixture was rejected with zero external rows.

161 automated tests cover the implemented boundaries. Model evaluation retains failures and abstentions. The next customer pilot compares historical cases, targeting at least 50 percent less active planner effort without missed service obligations. That is our measurement plan, not a claimed result.
